properties.name: The cost was an all-pairs betweenness recomputed on EVERY propagate_from call — not the node-type index and not the walk, both of which were measured and refuted first
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-09-11, closing `fact:design-regions-is-one-expensive-region-walk-per-seed-and-there-are-109-seeds`, whose SHAPE was right — N walks, one per seed — and whose named sub-cause was wrong.

THE ANSWER: `propagate_from`'s last act before returning is `self.design_network()?.betweenness()?` — it rebuilds the whole design network and runs an ALL-PAIRS betweenness over 4,176 nodes and 24,242 edges, on every call, purely to attach a centrality figure for ranking the impacted set. `design_regions` calls it 109 times.

    propagate_from, before        ~4,300 ms every call
    propagate_from, memoised       4,815 ms cold, then ~250 ms
    design_regions                >300 s (never returned) → 29.6 s

🛑 TWO HYPOTHESES WERE MEASURED AND REFUTED FIRST, and recording them is the point — both were plausible and both were mine:
  ① THE NODE-TYPE INDEX. `propagate_from` opens with `node_type_index()`, a scan of every node of every declared type, with 30 call sites and no memo. Memoised it — and `propagate_from` did not move. Then measured the scan directly: 7–85 ms per type, ~500 ms for all 28. It was never the cost. (The memo is kept: it is real, it is test-pinned, and 30 call sites pay it.)
  ② THE WALK. `impact_neighbors` looked like the per-seed cost. It uses indexed prefix scans over the adjacency column families, and a depth-1 radius is a handful of nodes.

⭐ THE MEASUREMENT THAT KILLED BOTH: calls #1 to #5 of `propagate_from`, no write between, came back 4705 / 4260 / 4227 / 4323 / 4284 ms. **Flat.** Anything a memo would fix drops after the first call; anything paid at startup does not recur. Flat-and-high means work redone every time, which pointed at the one line that does exactly that.

⚠️ AND A CONFOUND THAT NEARLY DERAILED IT: an early run measured `get_node` at 6,480 ms, which would have made the whole graph look slow. It is process hydration — the FIRST call of any kind costs ~6.7 s, and `get_node` was simply last in that sequence. Measuring `get_node` first separated startup from per-call cost; without that the numbers were unusable. `fact:every-cost-number-today-was-a-debug-build-and-the-live-store-is-7x-its-content` makes the same point: a number measures a whole setup.

THE FIX is the mechanism `dec:derived-scans-are-memoised-per-write-generation` already settled, and the argument is `con:a-sweep-builds-its-network-a-fixed-number-of-times` verbatim one tool over — *"the network has to be constructed once and interrogated N times"*. That Constraint binds `detect_defects` and does not reach `propagate_from`; whether it should be widened is a question for its owner, not something to assume.

BOUNDS: debug binary throughout; a release build is ~2.2x faster and would not have changed which line dominated. 29.6 s is a large improvement and is still slow for a tool billed as a check-in read — the remaining cost is the 109 walks themselves, now ~250 ms each, and whether that is acceptable is a judgement nobody has made.
properties.value: {"before":{"propagate_from_ms":4300,"design_regions":"never returned; >300s twice, >150s once"},"after":{"propagate_from_cold_ms":4815,"propagate_from_warm_ms":250,"design_regions_s":29.6},"refuted":{"node_type_index":"memoised anyway; a full build is ~500ms across 28 types (scan_nodes 7-85ms each), and propagate_from did not move","the_walk_itself":"impact_neighbors uses indexed prefix scans on CF_ADJ_IN/CF_ADJ_OUT; radius at depth 1 is a handful of nodes"},"discriminator":"propagate_from stayed ~4.3s on calls #1-#5 with no write between — unchanged by repetition, which rules out anything a memo would have fixed and anything paid at startup","startup_confound":"the first call of any kind costs ~6.7s of process hydration; measuring get_node FIRST separated it"}
